review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.issue: The inhibitor half-maximal crossing is near 60 micromolar, and the vehicle crossing near 20 rather than the stated 25. The ratio happens to remain three, but both numerical curve readings are off.

errors.quote: The inhibitor reduces the apparent affinity of the enzyme for the substrate.
errors.issue: Km is not generally the equilibrium substrate dissociation constant. State the increased substrate requirement without claiming an intrinsic affinity change from these curves.

errors.quote: ternary complex either cannot form or is catalytically dead
errors.issue: An inactive ESI complex can form in mixed/uncompetitive inhibition and ordinarily depresses the high-substrate asymptote. Inability to form ESI and formation of dead ESI are not equivalent to mutually exclusive binding in the stated simple competitive model.

errors.quote: confirm if the competitive model holds universally
errors.issue: A finite concentration matrix can support the model over tested conditions, not establish universal validity. Retain the tested domain, uncertainty and alternative-model limits.

errors.quote: to rule out aggregation-based artifactual inhibition
errors.issue: A single detergent condition does not rule out all aggregation artifacts. Include matched enzyme-compatibility controls and complementary concentration/physical or orthogonal-assay checks.

rationale: Recognizes the correct kinetic pattern and the need for independent localization, but inaccurate image readings and the dead-ESI equivalence materially weaken the scientific explanation. Experimental suggestions are useful after narrowing their claimed decisiveness.
reference_guardrails: All twelve complete final answers, the exact question, E1 packet, full sealed reference and synthetic figure were personally read. No paid judge, hidden reasoning or candidate web access was used.

The supplied shared asymptote is 100 nmol/min. Approximate half-maximal crossings are 20 and 60 micromolar, giving a threefold shift. At 300 micromolar the curves are about 94 and 83, not at the common asymptote. Accept reasonable approximate ranges; do not demand unreported fit precision.

Reference correction: the old required-concept/limitation text saying the shift cannot be quantified is too strong. The graphical shift can be estimated; exact fitted uncertainty and Ki remain unavailable. The updated paragraph already permits approximate 20-to-60 readings. Frozen original keys are preserved.

The synthetic ideal-MM/shared-asymptote premise is sufficient for the requested compatible kinetic classification. Proposed tests concern transfer to real data; no candidate must pretend experiments or error bars exist.

Reference correction: mutational effects are not necessary proof of active-site occupancy. Retained function, folding, direct binding and convergent contact evidence are needed; changes can be indirect. HDX or chemical-shift perturbations alone do not necessarily map ligand contacts.
Km generally combines binding and catalytic rates, not simply equilibrium Kd. Apparent affinity shorthand should not imply an intrinsic threefold Kd change.

Notation guardrail: in v=Vmax*S/(alpha*Km+alpha-prime*S), alpha=1+[I]/Ki and alpha-prime=1+[I]/Ki-prime. Pure competition has alpha-prime=1 and Ki-prime infinite. Other authors use a linkage alpha equal to a ratio of dissociation constants; accept a clearly defined alternative convention rather than penalizing a symbol alone.

An inactive ternary ESI complex is not equivalent to mutually exclusive ligand occupancy. Under the simple mixed model it decreases Vmax. A remote inhibitor can be kinetically competitive through mutual exclusion.

Incomplete recovery after dilution can be slow reversible dissociation or assay instability as well as irreversible inhibition. Competition binding and indirect mutational effects do not by themselves localize a pocket.
No actual enzyme experiments were run. The scores assess the written scientific explanation and proposed checks; this single unblinded AI review remains provisional and requires human review.

review_sources.title: Assay Guidance Manual: Mechanism of Action Assays for Enzymes
review_sources.scope: Search-indexed author-manual extracts corroborate kinetic competition without pocket identity and free-ligand/fit checks. Full page access returned a browser challenge; no claim of full-page inspection. Scoring primarily uses the supplied figure and explicit rate-law algebra; different alpha conventions are distinguished.
